commentary_title: Aframax market remains balanced as vessel availability improves
commentary_summary: Aframax utilisation rose to 90.6% in Week 45, up 1.3 percentage points YoY, while the tonne-mile index increased 15.8% YoY to 114.4, indicating that cargo demand remains supportive. However, utilisation declined 2.1 percentage points MoM, suggesting that improvements in vessel availability are currently outpacing demand growth. | Vessel productivity improved across several indicators during the month. Ballast tonnage at anchor declined by 0.6 mdwt on a four-week moving average basis, while anchored capacity fell sharply in the East. At the same time, ballast speeds remained elevated across both basins, supporting faster vessel circulation and effectively increasing available fleet supply. | Congestion trends also point to a more fluid market. Ballast tonnage at anchor in the Atlantic continued to trend lower compared with earlier in the year, while congestion in key regions such as China and the Pacific remained broadly contained. Although laden anchor days increased by 10.3%, the share of laden vessels declined in both the East and West, indicating that cargo delays have not materially tightened vessel availability.
